item.title: Matt Van Horn (@mvanhorn)
item.description:
Matt Van Horn
@mvanhorn

Co-founded June ("self-driving oven" acquired by @webergrills) & the co that became @Lyft. Building again, more soon. OS: @slashlast30days 67k★ @ppressdev 4.9k★

6.5k followers · 12 following

  • @mvanhorn
  • in/mattvanhorn

Popular Repository

last30days-skill 76.5k 6.8k
AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary

Other Repositories (Popular)

  • cli-printing-press 5.1k 548
    Every API has a secret identity. This finds it, absorbs every feature from every competing tool, then builds the GOAT CLI — designed for AI agents first, with SQLite sync, offline search, and compound insight commands.
  • printing-press-library 2.2k 646
    Official library of CLIs generated by the CLI Printing Press. Endorsed, tested, and community-contributed.
  • agentcookie 884 80
    Your agent runs on a Mac that isn't your daily driver. agentcookie keeps its sessions in sync with the Mac you actually browse on, continuously, encrypted over Tailscale, so OpenClaw, Hermes, or any other agent runtime wakes up authenticated. macOS, peer-to-peer, no cloud middleman.
  • agent-tincan 444 54
    Let your AI agents ask each other for help, over Tailscale. Wherever they run.
  • paperclip-plugin-telegram 106 43
    Bidirectional Telegram bot plugin for Paperclip - push notifications, bot commands, inline approve/reject buttons, reply routing
  • paperclip-plugin-acp 82 18
    ACP (Agent Client Protocol) runtime plugin for Paperclip - run Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI from any chat platform

Hey, I'm Matt Van Horn

Co-founded June ("self-driving oven," acquired by Weber) and the company that became Lyft. Building again, more soon. Open source: last30days 67k★ Printing Press 4.9k★

Building

  • last30days - AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web.
  • Printing Press - Generates ship-ready CLIs for any API with a research, build, polish, publish loop, agent-first design with SQLite sync and offline search.
  • Printing Press Library - Official library of CLIs generated by the Printing Press, endorsed, tested, and community-contributed.
  • agentcookie - Syncs your agent's browser sessions to your daily-driver Mac, encrypted over Tailscale, so any agent runtime wakes up authenticated.
  • Agent Tincan - Lets your AI agents ask each other for help over your own Tailscale network, so Grok Bot, Muse, Codex, Claude Code, ChatGPT and Claude can borrow each other's powers. Agents set it up themselves.

👋 余，t8y2

总角之年，初触代码，不过稚子嬉戏耳。不意廿载倏忽，竟以此为业。其间由前端而后端，由桌面而数据，所学愈广，所未知者亦愈多。然探索之心，未尝稍减。

能亲操键，亦善假 AI 之力。或 Rust，或 Go，或 TypeScript，前后端皆涉，桌面应用亦多。 数据库自 MySQL 至 DuckDB 靡不摆弄，框架自 Vue 至 Tauri 皆有交付。不拘工具，唯问产出。

性 INTJ，讷言敏行。不尚空谈，不好著文，但以代码见真章。每有所思，辄夜半起而操键，不知东方之既白。

躬耕开源，DBX、Motty、Viva、UniHub、PolarisDesk 皆心血之作。 每成一器，必倾力而为。从无到有，其间自有乐趣；倘有用户称善，则足矣。

造物而已，尽心而已。

🚧 Building

  • DBX — 轻量级跨平台数据库管理工具，支持 100+ 数据库，桌面端 / CLI / Docker / 内置 AI
  • Motty — 原生桌面 SSH 工作台，终端 / SFTP / 端口转发 / VNC-RDP / AI 助手同处一窗，Go + Viva，无 WebView

    Production-ready Claude Code plugins: skills, hooks, agents, slash commands, and MCP templates.

Florian Bruniaux

Official Claude Community Ambassador · Paris
Sharing practical ways to work with Claude through open-source guides and community work.
View my Ambassador profile ↗

I’m a hands-on Fractional Chief AI Officer and former CTO, CTPO and VP Engineering. I help leaders choose where to invest in AI, then work directly with engineering and product teams in their repositories.

I specialise in harness and context engineering. I build the shared instructions, tools, permissions and checks that teams use to develop and review software with Claude Code and Codex.

  • Claude Code Ultimate Guide. I wrote it and still maintain it. It includes workflows, templates and exercises teams can use in their own codebases.
  • RTK. I was its first contributor, wrote most of its early code and later focused on promoting the project. RTK trims command output so coding agents spend fewer tokens on routine tasks.

Portfolio · Work with me

📬 Blog & Guides

I write about AI-assisted engineering: how agents get their context, how teams verify their work, and what the whole workflow costs.

All articles · All practical guides

Recent articles

Published Article
Oct 14, 2026 5 AI code reviewers, 1 repository, and what developers did next
Oct 14, 2026 Turn recurring review comments into tested controls
Oct 14, 2026 A green review is not a merge gate
Oct 3, 2026 Lean and AI: follow the work until it reaches the user
Sep 30, 2026 How to read a token-compression benchmark

Published series

25 articles and guides across four series. Each series page gives the full reading order.

Series Parts Focus
Engineering the Review Loop 8 Local checks, independent review, bounded corrections and merge evidence.
The Real Cost of AI 9 Task costs, ROI claims, productivity evidence, FinOps and provider dependence.
Context Engineering 6 Context drift, instruction systems, tool choices and portability.
Designing Agent Output 2 Flow Lean skills, output styles and checks for their actual behavior.

Guides & reports

  • Claude Code Ultimate Guide: a continuously maintained reference for AI-assisted development. Companion pages cover AI FinOps and token-saving tools.
  • Claude Cowork Guide: AI workflows for knowledge workers and non-technical users.
  • Claude Code security: the attack surface few teams audit: review hooks, connected tools and the permissions they receive.
  • Moving the memory observer to a local model: a measured claude-mem case study covering request constraints, timeouts and output quality.
  • Context engineering: the L0-to-L5 playbook: choose context controls according to the failure you observe.
  • One source configures Claude Code and Codex: shared instructions, immutable releases and skill routing. English · Français.
  • From code to merge: my Dev With AI talk, with slides, examples and section recaps. English · Français.
  • Dev With AI 2026: conference synthesis and an illustrated report with a TL;DR for each talk. English guide · Guide français · Full report EN · Dossier complet FR.

If you land here from a guide page or an article, starring the repo is the best way to see when something new ships.

Current Focus

  • Fractional AI leadership. I work with leadership and product teams on AI priorities, investment decisions and adoption.
  • Harness and context engineering. I build shared instructions, tools, permissions, tests and review workflows for coding agents.
  • Open source. I maintain the Claude Code Ultimate Guide and build tools such as ctxharness.
  • Training and speaking. I run hands-on workshops for teams, contribute to the Dev with AI community and share what I learn in talks and interviews.

What I Build

Claude Code Ultimate Guide

Comprehensive resource for AI-assisted development with Claude Code. Documentation-as-product: 473 quiz questions (17 categories), 13 whitepapers (566 pages, FR+EN), 57 recap cards, threat database with 166 catalogued malicious skills/CVEs. 6,000+ stars · 790+ forks · cc.bruniaux.com

RTK - Rust Token Killer

CLI proxy that compresses the output of common dev commands (Git, GitHub CLI, Cargo, pnpm, Vitest, Playwright, Docker, Kubernetes) before it reaches the agent. The project reports 60-90% fewer tokens on that output; whole-task studies are collected on cc.bruniaux.com/token-savings. 82,000+ stars · First contributor and main contributor in Q1 2026, then evangelist · rtk-ai.app

Agent Router

Local Rust CLI that picks the model, effort and skills for each phase of a Claude Code or Codex task (plan, execute, verify) and explains why. Limits are checked before scoring, decisions replay to the same receipt, and nothing runs without an approved digest. Experimental: offline routing works; no measured cost gain is claimed yet. Public repository · Build from source with Rust 1.85+ · Source-available (FSL-1.1-ALv2)

Search Console MCP

Connect Claude, Codex, and other MCP clients to Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, GA4, CrUX, and public-page analysis through 81 structured tools. Open the bilingual product site · Documentation · GitHub · PyPI

Worktree Sweep

Read-only Rust CLI for macOS to inventory Git worktrees, check commit relationships against selected refs, and inspect local files. A commit can be integrated while untracked or ignored files still need preservation. Backup, restore and removal are unavailable in this MVP. wt-sweep.bruniaux.com · Source-available (FSL-1.1-ALv2)

StarMapper

Map any GitHub repository's stargazers on an interactive world map. Paste a repo URL, get a live geocoded map with clustering, country stats, and an embeddable badge. Next.js + MapLibre + Neon Postgres. starmapper.bruniaux.com

Open-source galaxy

Background

As Founding AI Engineer at Méthode Aristote from July 2025 to October 2026, I built the initial EdTech codebase from scratch, developed the team’s AI harness and trained product builders to contribute to production. I shared the review workflow in From code to merge. Our collaboration continued on a freelance basis after the salaried role ended.

AI since 2017: NLP and predictive ML in production at Q°emotion and eXplain (semantic search, sentiment scoring, ~30M articles processed). Generative and agentic AI daily since 2025.

12+ years: Developer → Team Lead → EM → VP Engineering → CTO → back to hands-on by choice.

Why hands-on? After a decade leading teams (4-150 people, managed up to 30 engineers), I deliberately stepped back to sharpen my technical edge. Leadership is more effective when grounded in current engineering reality. In the first 3 months of 2026, that bet produced 10+ open-source projects, 5,000+ stars on my own, plus core contributions to RTK (82,000+ stars).

Tech:

    Demonstrate end to end Agentic SDLC on Microsoft stack, From a Teams meeting (WorkIQ) intent to automated implementation and then Azure deployment. Powered by GitHub Copilot SDK.
  • awesome-ai-native 117 20
    Learn to master GitHub Copilot with AI Native Development practices

Daniel Meppiel

I work on the methodology and tools for building software with AI agents at enterprise scale.

I'm a Software Global Black Belt at Microsoft and the creator of APM (Agent Package Manager) — the open-source tool teams use to manage AI agent configurations the way they manage code. I designed the PROSE framework for writing agent specifications that hold up in production, and I wrote The Agentic SDLC Handbook to put the whole methodology in one place.

Before Microsoft: GitHub, Sonar, four years as CTO and co-founder of WeGaw, and earlier engineering work at CERN.

🔭 What I'm working on now

  • 📘 The Agentic SDLC Handbook — released as a pre-release edition; shipping refinements and new case studies continuously.
  • 📦 microsoft/apm — Agent Package Manager. apm install, apm compile. The 2-command pattern Fortune 500 teams are adopting.
  • 📐 microsoft/agentrc — Get your repo ready for AI. The companion convention for instrumenting codebases.
  • 🧬 genesis — an architect's discipline for designing agentic systems across primitives (skills, agents, instructions, orchestrators, plans). Markdown that steers an LLM is code — design it before you write it. Portable across Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex.
  • ✍️ The AI-Native Mind — short essays on what AI-native development looks like once the demo ends.

Updated monthly. If this is stale, I owe you a coffee.

🧰 Pinned work — the throughline

Three tools → the methodology → proof of range.

Project Why it's here
microsoft/apm Agent Package Manager. How AI agent capabilities are packaged, versioned, and shared across teams.
microsoft/agentrc The convention for getting a codebase ready to be worked on by AI agents.
genesis An architect's discipline for designing agentic systems — across skills, agents, instructions, orchestrators, plans. Harness-portable.
agentic-sdlc-handbook The book that ties all three together — written using the methodology it teaches.
awesome-ai-native The PROSE framework, distilled. Start here if you're a practitioner.
meeting-2-code End-to-end proof: Teams meeting → shipped Azure feature, fully agentic.
oracle-mcp-server MCP server for very large Oracle schemas — serious engineering outside the AI-native bubble.

🎙️ Speaking & writing

I talk about what changes — for the org, the codebase, and the developer's day — when AI coding agents become a real part of how software gets built.

  • 📕 The Agentic SDLC Handbook — free online, PDF, EPUB
  • 🧠 theainativemind.com — newsletter & essays
  • 💬 Want me to talk to your team or at your event? DM me on LinkedIn.

A note on the journey

I don't think anyone has this fully figured out yet — including me. APM, agentrc, and genesis were born from ingenuity and breaking things, and they're evolving fast. If you're building in this space, I'd genuinely love to compare notes.

→ The fastest way to stay in the loop: subscribe to the handbook updates.

Opinions here are my own and don't represent my employer.

Other Repositories (Pinned)

  • groktocrawl 89 14
    Self-hosted, API-compatible Firecrawl alternative with Agent endpoint. MIT license. One docker compose up.
  • artifact-pyramids 12 2
    The Artifact Pyramid: progressive disclosure for what agents produce — a structured methodology for organizing AI agent research outputs across three layers of fidelity.
  • hermes-cashew 19 2
    Memory provider for Hermes Agent to work with rajkripal/cashew
  • SlopSearX 15 7
    Self-hosted search and research infrastructure for AI agents. Query web and specialist sources through MCP, run durable research jobs, and monitor results with replayable change events. SearXNG-compatible HTTP API.
  • codereview 4 0
    Deterministic, bounded AI code review harness with CLI and GitHub Actions integration

Magnus Hedemark

Engineering executive, AI practitioner, and open-source contributor. I build agentic systems and run much of the infrastructure myself so my ideas stay connected to what actually works.

I keep a compass of what guides me. It's the most honest thing I've written.

What I build

agent-skills - A growing open-source library of reusable AI agent capabilities, from software delivery and product strategy to business operations, research, and creative work. It also covers governance, evaluations, production operations, operating economics, and multi-agent collaboration. Built around the open Agent Skills format for portability across frameworks.

groktocrawl - A self-hosted web data and research platform compatible with the Firecrawl v2 API. Scraping, crawling, structured extraction, browser automation, monitors, semantic retrieval, an autonomous research agent, and MCP in one Docker deployment. MIT licensed.

SlopSearX - A stateless, agent-first meta search engine with a SearXNG-compatible API, MCP tools, and a human search portal. Self-hosted search with structured outputs and control over how agents consume the web. A Rust rewrite is in progress.

codereview - An experimental AI code-review harness with deterministic planning, bounded specialist reviews, and auditable reports. The CLI is read-only, with publishing limited to review previews.

Wordgames - Self-hosted daily word puzzles with an accessible browser interface and a Rust publishing backend. Built for playing, extending, and running yourself. Play online.

Tools and methods

hermes-cashew - A Hermes Agent memory-provider plugin integrating Cashew's local thought graph, semantic search, automatic recall, and consolidation. Bridges the gap between what an agent knows and what it remembers. Maintainer.

hermes-SkillOpt - A controlled skill-optimization workflow for Hermes Agent, inspired by Microsoft Research's SkillOpt. It runs skills against tasks, proposes bounded edits, and validates them on held-out tasks before acceptance.

artifact pyramids - A methodology I designed for structuring AI research outputs. Progressive disclosure from a one-line summary to deep dossiers, built so agents and humans can share the same artifacts.

Community

RDUMesh - A community mesh network I co-founded covering the Research Triangle area. Real infrastructure, real nodes.

What I write

Two sites, two audiences.

magnus919.com - For engineers. Deep dives on agent memory systems, RAG architecture, self-hosted infrastructure, and the hard parts of building persistent AI systems.

groktop.us - For technology leaders. Strategy and field notes on AI transformation, earned autonomy, organizational design, governance, and what it takes to put agentic systems into real work.

Pick your adventure.

How I build

I maintain a homelab that runs most of the infrastructure I build and write about. Self-hosted search (SlopSearX), agent backends (LightRAG, hermes-cashew), mesh network repeaters, and the usual staples (Traefik, Grafana, Postgres, a NAS). I believe in operating what you build. It's the fastest way to find the edge cases.

Find me

LinkedIn for my professional work and leadership background. My longer-form writing lives at groktop.us and magnus919.com.

You can also find me on Bluesky.
